sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球海事商船注册旗国、借鉴特拉华州公司法的非公开发行实体

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Chartering and Operation of Offshore Platform Support Ships

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid: US-derived common law corporate framework (Business Corporations Act modeled on the Delaware General Corporation Law), recognized customary law under the RMI Constitution, with statutory civil law elements
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Compact of Free Association between the Republic of the Marshall Islands and the United States of America (1986; Amended Compact 2003)
Hague Convention of 5 October 1961 Abolishing the Requirement of Legalisation for Foreign Public Documents (Apostille Convention), in force for the RMI
New York Convention on the Recognition and Enforcement of Foreign Arbitral Awards (1958), applicable to international offshore charter and vessel leasing disputes

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Business Corporations Act (BCA), 31 MIRC Chapter 1, as amended by the Business Corporations (Amendment) Acts 2020 and 2021; Anti-Money Laundering and Countering the Financing of Terrorism Act, 2020 (AML/CFT Act 2020), as amended; Banking Act, 2011 (31 MIRC Chapter 2); Insurance (Regulation and Supervision) Act, 2011; Registrar of Corporations Directive on Beneficial Ownership (2021) mandating a government-access UBO register for all BCA corporations; APG mutual evaluation remediation commitments (2022-2025)
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access: the Beneficial Ownership Declaration is filed with the Registrar of Corporations and is accessible to the RMI Financial Intelligence Unit, the Banking Commissioner, domestic law enforcement, the Maritime Administrator (for shipowning entities), and authorized foreign competent authorities via mutual legal assistance; it is not included in the public registry index, which discloses only director and officer details

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney appointing the RMI Resident Registered Agent and Authorized Signatories
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Parent entity/founding shareholders executed before a Notary Public in the document's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (documents from Apostille Convention states) OR Consular Legalization at the RMI Consular Mission / RMI Embassy (Washington D.C.) for non-Convention documents

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / registry extract of the parent company (shipowner or chartering lessor)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry of the parent company's home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization (RMI Embassy/Consulate) plus notarial certification of the translator's signature where applicable

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copies of passports and proof of residential address of intended directors, shareholders and ultimate beneficial owners
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public (home jurisdiction) with issuing-state attestation where the notary is not self-authenticating
RMI Registrar of Corporations (receiving authority), prepared and countersigned by the licensed registered agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Internal statutory filing to the government-access UBO register; signatory notarization required where the declaration is executed outside the RMI

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter, escrow authorization (Escrow_Maritime) and P&I/OSV insurance evidence for the chartered offshore supply vessel program
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Obligatory bank, escrow agent or P&I Club of the vessel operator/lessor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization plus Hague Apostille / consular legalization where required by the RMI receiving bank or the Maritime Administrator

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, officers, charter counterparties and escrow beneficiaries against the OFAC SDN List (including the 50% rule), UN Security Council Consolidated List, RMI domestic sanctions and watchlists, APG/FATF public statements, and EU/UK financial sanctions applicable to the USD Swift_Wire and Escrow_Maritime payment rails. Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) and close associates require enhanced due diligence (source of wealth and funds verification), board-level approval for high-risk jurisdiction nexus, adverse media screening, and re-screening at least every 90 days and upon any trigger event (shareholding change, director change, new charter counterparty, or sanctions-list update). No beneficial ownership nominee masking is permitted at or above the 25% threshold for a BCA engaged in offshore vessel leasing.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Official RMI Corporate Registry Portal administered by the Office of the Registrar of Corporations, Majuro (electronic name search, reservation and filing accepted via the Registrar's e-portal and through licensed RMI registered agents; direct counters at the Registry, Majuro)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Filing and registration language is English; corporate names must be expressed in the Roman/Latin alphabet (the RMI uses a 24-letter Latin-script orthography for Marshallese, and English is the operative commercial language). The name must be capable of exact search and indexing in the Registry's digital index; where a coined name originates in a non-Latin script, a distinct transliteration in Roman characters must be submitted and cannot be phonetically confusing with an existing name. The name must include as the last element 'Corporation', 'Incorporated', 'Limited', or the abbreviations 'Corp.', 'Inc.', 'Ltd.', or words of like import in another language, as required under the Business Corporations Act.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Names identical or confusingly similar (including phonetic variants and abbreviations) to an existing RMI registered entity or recognized foreign registered name

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Marshall Islands Business Corporation Act, MIRC Title 33, Chapter 1, as amended, including Sections 33.101 (incorporation), 33.201 (board of directors), 33.301 (registered agent and office), 33.601 (directors), and 33.801 (officers).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Marshall Islands Business Registry, Office of the Registrar of Corporations, Majuro Atoll
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Marshall Islands Non-Resident Domestic Corporation)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is required; the authorized share capital is set in the Articles of Incorporation, and any subscription proceeds may be held in escrow pending corporate use and governance approval.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that this Corporation subscribes to and ratifies the issuance of the shares set forth in the Articles of Incorporation, and the board duly adopts the Articles and all subordinate bylaws. RESOLVED, that the registered office and registered agent named in the Articles are approved as the statutory address and statutory agent of the Corporation. RESOLVED, that the incorporators shall serve as interim directors, and the following officers are appointed: President, Secretary, and Chief Financial Officer, each with full authority to execute charter contracts, open bank accounts, and obtain all vessel and environmental licenses necessary for the offshore supply vessel leasing business.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Marshall Islands Business Registry (Online Name Search and Reservation Portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation application through the Registry's online portal or in notarized paper form. Include the proposed corporate name containing 'Corporation', 'Company', 'Limited', or an approved abbreviation. Pay the name reservation fee and obtain a Reservation Certificate.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name and suffix election
Proof of non-identical name search result
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for similarity or prohibited wording, file a formal appeal to the Registrar of Corporations within 10 business days or submit an amended name to re-run the clearance process.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Marshall Islands Business Registry, Office of the Registrar of Corporations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute Articles of Incorporation in English, designating the corporation as a non-resident domestic entity, stating authorized shares, appointing the registered agent and registered office, and setting out the corporate purpose for offshore supply vessel leasing. Notarize all executory signatures and submit the original and two copies with the statutory filing fee schedule.
required_dossiers: Consent of Registered Agent to the appointment
Passport or ID copy of each incorporator
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a deficiency letter, correct the listed defects, renotarize where necessary, and resubmit within 15 business days to preserve the original filing priority. If resubmission is incomplete, a new priority date and a resubmission penalty may apply.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Payment of Government Fees and Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Marshall Islands Business Registry, Payment and Certificate Section
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Remit the official government incorporation fee by SWIFT transfer or approved debit to the Registry's designated trust account. Attach the payment remittance advice to the filed Articles. After verification, the Registrar will allocate a file number and issue the formal Certificate of Incorporation and corporate seal.
required_dossiers: SWIFT or bank transfer remittance advice
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If payment cannot be matched, submit a payment trace letter from the remitting bank; the Registry will confirm receipt and reissue the certificate without an additional government charge where bank proof is furnished.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration of Initial Directors and Officers and Corporate Governance Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Marshall Islands Business Registry, Corporate Records Section
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the initial director and officer consents, biographical notices, and the organizational resolutions of the incorporators adopting bylaws, approving the registered office, and ratifying the share subscription. The Registrar will update the public corporate register accordingly.
required_dossiers: Consent to Act as Director for each initial director
Consent to Act as Officer for each initial officer
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any biographical notice or consent is queried, provide a notarized English translation or an amended consent form within 10 business days; if a consent is missing, obtain a fresh signed consent and request a register rectification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Marshall Islands Flag Registration and Vessel Operating License
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Marshall Islands Maritime Administrator (MIMA) administered by International Registries, Inc.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for Marshall Islands flag registration of each offshore supply vessel. Provide tonnage measurement certificates, ownership or bareboat charter evidence, and complete the statutory safety and security survey. Obtain the Certificate of Registry and the Offshore Supply Vessel Compliance Certificate under the IMO OSV Code.
required_dossiers: Application for Vessel Registration on the Marshall Islands Register
Evidence of ownership or bareboat charter authority
ISPS Ship Security Plan and Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a flag-state survey reveals deficiencies, submit a Corrective Action Plan and arrange a re-inspection; once all findings are resolved, the Maritime Administrator will issue the registry and safety certificates with effect from the application date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Environmental and Occupational Clearance for Shore and Vessel Operations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Marshall Islands Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) and the Occupational Health and Safety Bureau, Ministry of Employment
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain environmental clearance for any onshore office or port base covering wastewater, waste handling, and air emissions, and maintain current MARPOL certificates for the vessel. Submit fire safety certificates, structural load inspections, and OSH clearance for all workplaces and shore facilities.
required_dossiers: EPA Registration Application or Environmental Management Plan
Workplace Occupational Health and Safety Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the EPA returns a deficiency list, file the required environmental studies or mitigation commitments within 20 business days; for occupational clearance, implement corrective fire or load safety measures and obtain a re-inspection certificate.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Marshall Islands Maritime Administrator (MIMA), Marine Safety and Survey Department
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Marshall Islands Offshore Supply Vessel Operating License and Certificate of Vessel Safety Compliance

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) of the Republic of the Marshall Islands
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registered marine environmental activity requiring an Environmental Compliance Statement; full EIA report not applicable to mobile offshore supply vessel operations
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Oil discharge shall not exceed 15 ppm under MARPOL Annex I; sewage discharge must meet Annex IV distance and control rules; garbage must be managed under Annex V; fuel sulfur content must remain below 0.50% m/m outside Emission Control Areas; ballast water must meet IMO BWM Convention standards; any regulated wastewater discharge requires prior EPA authorization or applicable MARPOL operational reporting.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate issued by the certified fire marshal for the onshore office and port base, structural load inspection clearance for piers and support facilities, and workplace occupational health and safety clearance for all crew members and shore maintenance personnel under the applicable Marshall Islands labor and marine safety regulations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Marshall Islands Revenue and Tax Division, Ministry of Finance, Republic of the Marshall Islands (Majuro); corporate registry administered by the RMI Registrar of Corporations through licensed registered agents via the RMI Registry electronic portal (https://www.rmi-registry.com); no separate e-filing tax portal, filings are paper-based.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign-owned non-resident domestic corporation: (1) engage an RMI-licensed registered agent; (2) file Articles of Incorporation under the Business Corporations Act 1990 electing non-resident domestic corporation status (all shareholders must be non-residents and the corporation must transact no business in the RMI); (3) obtain the Certificate of Incorporation, which is the statutory corporate identifier (no separate TIN is issued); (4) submit a Gross Revenue Tax (GRT) registration or exemption notification to the Revenue and Tax Division to establish the GRT account status; (5) no VAT/TIN registration is possible because the RMI imposes no VAT or GST; (6) if flag-state registration is desired, register the vessel with the RMI Maritime Administrator through its authorized agent.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: RMI law has no IRC-style check-the-box regime. The controlling election is the non-resident domestic corporation designation under the Business Corporations Act 1990, which renders the entity exempt from RMI income tax and the Gross Revenue Tax. The election must be maintained by ensuring non-resident shareholding and the absence of RMI-source business activity; revocation to taxable resident status is permitted. Hybrid mismatch elections under OECD BEPS Action 2 are not codified in RMI domestic law; however, the interaction with a shareholder's domestic classification (e.g., US Form 8832 check-the-box) and the entity's separate juridical personality under RMI law must be analyzed by counsel to avoid inadvertent double non-taxation or treaty-shopping allegations.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Gross Revenue Tax (GRT) and Import Duty — no VAT or GST in the RMI
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: GRT imposes no de minimis turnover threshold: any person carrying on business within the RMI must register and account for GRT on gross revenue. Non-resident domestic corporations deriving no RMI-source revenue are statutorily exempt. Import duty is assessed in USD on physical importation of goods into the RMI under the applicable customs tariff schedule; services and offshore charter hire are outside the import duty base.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No e-invoicing, real-time fiscal clearance, API connectivity, or digital stamping mandate exists in the RMI. GRT taxpayers must issue standard commercial invoices and retain books and records for a minimum of six years. Customs import declarations are filed with RMI Customs; export of services requires no customs clearance.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: The RMI has no VAT or GST, so no VAT zero-rating or refund mechanism exists. Instead, export-derived receipts are exempt at the statutory level: (i) the Gross Revenue Tax Act exempts gross revenue from goods and services exported for use outside the RMI; and (ii) the Income Tax Act excludes non-resident domestic corporations from tax on income sourced outside the RMI. The bareboat or time charter of an RMI-flag offshore supply vessel to a non-resident charterer for operations exclusively in international waters qualifies as an export service, provided the charterer is non-resident, charter-hire payments originate from outside the RMI, and the vessel makes no calls at RMI domestic ports during the tax period.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: RMI Maritime Administrator: valid Certificate of Registry (Vessel Registration Certificate) and Minimum Safe Manning Document
Executed bareboat charter party or time charter party agreement
Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT MT103 evidencing foreign-currency charter receipts
Vessel movement log or certificate of no-call at RMI domestic ports for the relevant tax period
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Revenue and Tax Division may audit the non-resident status and foreign-source substantiation of a non-resident domestic corporation. Failure to sustain the exemption may result in reclassification as a resident domestic corporation, retrospective income tax and 3% Gross Revenue Tax assessments for up to six years, statutory civil penalties and monthly interest accruing from the due date on any underpaid tax, fines under the Business Corporations Act for status misdeclaration, potential dissolution of the corporation, and criminal prosecution for fraudulent exemption claims under the Income Tax Act. Retrospective clawback of GRT exemptions applies on a gross-revenue basis, not net of expenses.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The Republic of the Marshall Islands (RMI) does not maintain a domestic central bank or issue a national currency. The de facto monetary and settlement authority is the United States Federal Reserve System as the issuer of the U.S. dollar, which is legal tender in RMI. Domestic financial institution supervision and licensing are conducted by the Marshall Islands Banking Commission in conjunction with the RMI Ministry of Finance, Banking and Postal Services.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The RMI has no statutory foreign-exchange control regime because the U.S. dollar is the sole legal tender. Both current-account and capital-account transactions are freely convertible within the dollar clearing system. Profit remittances, dividends, intercompany payments, and capital liquidations are not subject to foreign-exchange permits or central bank conversion requirements. The only transaction-level friction is anti-money-laundering (AML) reporting and record-keeping, including the obligation to report currency or monetary-instrument movements above the U.S. $10,000 threshold. There are no exchange controls prohibiting the repatriation of charter revenue or the disposal of vessel assets.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory export-proceeds surrender obligation in the RMI. Offshore supply-vessel leasing and charter-hire receipts may be retained in U.S. dollars indefinitely without mandatory conversion. The effective surrender ratio is zero percent and there is no legislated deadline for bringing export receipts onshore. Nevertheless, receipts above USD 10,000 in cash must be reported in accordance with the Banking Act 2003 and the RMI Money Laundering and Proceeds of Crime Act; wire transfers must be supported by underlying charter-party or sub-charter documentation to satisfy due diligence.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of Guam - Marshall Islands Branch (Majuro)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low / Not viable as a primary clearing rail. The RMI has no e-money institution or financial-technology EMI licensing framework under domestic law. Digital-only offshore banks and non-resident EMIs cannot become direct participants in the RMI local clearing system and are not recognized by the Marshall Islands Banking Commission as regulated depository institutions. An offshore EMI may only be used as a supplemental treasury-intake vehicle where its parent bank holds a U.S. or comparable OECD license, but it cannot substitute for a physical commercial bank account in RMI for capital escrow, marine-charter settlements, or documentary letters of credit. RMI banks apply enhanced due diligence when non-resident fintech intermediaries are used because of the opacity of downstream customer identification.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a non-resident Business Corporation, physical appearance at the banking branch is generally required for at least one director, the corporate secretary, or the authorized signatory with full power to bind the account. The Marshall Islands Banking Commission's post-2020 regulatory posture has caused Bank of Marshall Islands and Bank of Guam to require an in-person KYC/beneficial-ownership interview in Majuro or Ebeye. Remote account opening is occasionally available for low-risk structures if the application is supported by an Apostille-certified corporate extract, a Medallion Signature Guarantee, and a video conference with a compliance officer; however, remote opening is unavailable for politically exposed persons, bearer-share structures, or jurisdictions listed by the Financial Action Task Force. In all cases, beneficial owners holding more than 10% of the entity must be disclosed.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Bearer-share authorization or nominee-director arrangement commonly retained in the offshore corporate registry file, which may be treated as an unexplained beneficial-ownership structure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A current certificate of incumbency issued by the registered agent, a complete beneficial-ownership register naming every individual owning more than 10%, a board resolution expressly waiving bearer-share entitlement in the account application, and original passport copies of all ultimate beneficial owners backed by notarized identity verification and a source-of-wealth statement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Business activity is high-risk 'offshore marine chartering' where revenue derives from foreign-flag vessels operating outside RMI waters, creating uncertainty as to the underlying charterer and cargo or voyage pattern.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed time or voyage charter-party agreements for the leased offshore supply vessels, vessel classification and registration certificates, the ISM/ISPS certification of the operating fleet, a detailed operating-plan narrative, and the contractual flow-of-funds chart showing charter-hire payment chains from the ultimate charterer to the RMI entity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The non-resident entity is tax-exempt and may be perceived as a shell corporation lacking economic substance in the RMI.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A substance declaration demonstrating physical administrative presence in the form of a service agreement with a RMI licensed corporate service provider, board meeting minutes held in RMI, bank signatory authority held by directors physically present, and evidence of commercial substance such as vessel ownership records, lease contracts, operational insurance policies, and a documented treasury-management function centered in Majuro.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant capital injections into the RMI Business Corporation should be executed exclusively in U.S. dollars by SWIFT MT103 from the shareholder's account at a regulated bank to the designated Capital Escrow or Operational Account at a RMI commercial bank. The originating bank must include the corporate name, the vessel-identity reference, and the narrative 'Equity contribution to MH_BC offshore supply-vessel leasing under ISIC 5222'. The remitter must be the actual beneficial owner or a named shareholder; third-party payments are prohibited unless supported by a notarized subordination agreement and source-of-funds declaration. Correspondent clearing should route through a U.S. dollar correspondent bank using the receiving bank's BIC, and the RMI bank must verify that the funds do not originate from a sanctioned jurisdiction prior to crediting. A certified copy of the bank credit advice, the SWIFT MT103 execution report, and the source-of-funds letter must be retained in the corporate funds file.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade disbursements for offshore supply-vessel chartering and operations should be effected through SWIFT MT103 for hire settlements, sub-charter payments, crew payroll, fuel, port fees, and marine insurance premiums. For vessel acquisition, shipyard repairs, or large equipment purchases, an irrevocable documentary letter of credit issued under UCP600 is the preferred clearing rail, with settlement at sight or by deferred payment and presentation of the full marine transport document set, including the vessel invoice, delivery certificate, bill of sale, and classification-society compliance certificate. Interbank reimbursements above USD 250,000 should be routed with SWIFT MT202COV to preserve end-to-end originator data. No cash or bearer-instrument payments are permitted for any disbursement connected to vessel chartering. All outward remittances must map to the underlying charter-party or supplier invoice and must carry a purpose code consistent with cross-border maritime transportation services.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable U.S. dollar foreign-exchange forwards against currencies such as EUR, AUD, NZD, and SGD with a licensed counterparty bank, documented under an ISDA 1998 FX and Currency Options Definitions or 2002 Master Agreement.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) referenced to regulated emerging-market currencies executed offshore outside the RMI because the RMI does not regulate a domestic FX forward market; settlement is in U.S. dollars and requires no RMI exchange-control approval.

Cross-currency swaps (mark-to-market exchange of principal and interest between USD and relevant invoice currencies) under an ISDA Credit Support Annex, with a threshold to restrict counterparty credit risk to a maximum of 25% of the entity's consolidated treasury exposure.

Option-type instruments, including plain-vanilla USD call/EUR put and USD put/EUR call options with maturities matching the charter-hire receivable cycle, provided the counterparty is a U.S., EU, or Australian licensed bank with RMI-compatible AML/CFT documentation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Report (Statement of Information) for Business Corporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Marshall Islands Business and Corporate Law Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before March 31, unless a different date is designated in the corporation's registration certificate; newly incorporated entities must file the first Annual Report for the year following incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late penalty of 10% of the annual fee for any overdue payment; continued non-compliance beyond six months exposes the corporation to administrative strike-off, forfeiture of legal existence, and inability to enforce contracts or utilize the Marshall Islands registered name.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: None imposed by the Marshall Islands Business Corporations Act for a non-resident exempted business corporation; audit becomes compulsory only if the corporation is licensed to conduct business in the Marshall Islands, is listed on a recognized exchange, or becomes subject to a domestic banking, insurance, or public-interest activity threshold, none of which apply to an offshore supply vessel leasing entity.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) as adopted by the entity; US GAAP is also acceptable for United States-connected reporting purposes. No Marshall Islands domestic GAAP is prescribed for non-resident business corporations.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Annual Report serves as the annual confirmation of registered agent, registered office, directors, and officers. All share transfers must be recorded in the Register of Members and communicated to the registered agent. The registered agent performs a refreshed UBO and AML/KYC verification at least annually, or upon a triggered event such as a share transfer or beneficial ownership change. No separate UBO register is filed with the Registrar of Corporations; UBO data remains securely maintained by the registered agent and is produced only to lawful regulatory request.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 400 - 800 annual registered agent and registered office service fees
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500 - 6,000 if voluntarily contracted; no statutory audit is required for a non-resident exempted business corporation
